conclusion.concreteFailure: Both recorded product-admitted Darwin tuples reach strict P09 and fail. x64 additionally fails the compiler-default original-image witness; both architectures retain after-check and already-open-writer successful mutations followed by A markers and ordinary exit.
conclusion.feasibility: No defensible deployable continuous same-path/same-inode custody primitive or narrow implementation is established by these sources and artifacts. A matching future native observation venue is necessary to evaluate any concrete candidate, but matching/moving runners is not the missing fix: both counterexamples already occurred on admitted tuples.

strictInvariantAndFixBoundary.invariant: Before any selected library/payload instruction, retain a real native protection tied to the same selected path/inode and original PID/audit token/birth/parent/group/session. It must remain effective against the actual descriptor opened before launch and through the one original release/resume and lifetime. If mutation succeeds, the independent protection must cause signal termination before every selected marker; if denied, the frozen alternative requires genuine ETXTBSY and exact normal A.
strictInvariantAndFixBoundary.custodyNotObservation: Retaining a read-only descriptor and sampling/hash-validating its bytes is not a demonstrated continuous guard. Another pre-resume comparison cannot fill the post-comparison interval or substitute for retained protection.
strictInvariantAndFixBoundary.immutableCopyLimit: Executing an immutable private copy or alternate inode could be a different design, but it changes the frozen original-path/same-inode/existing-writer adversary. It is not a valid narrow correction to this P09 contract and is not proposed here.
